ctx.x: That's just what the entertainers and musicians called it, "Paradise Valley", Like what it meant was when everybody got off of work, they all congregated at that block and everybody, you know, talked their thing and whatnot and so forth and so on.

So Kelly Martin, it was a 12-piece band, and Al McKibbon was in the band and Kelly was the leader and we had chorus girls and they'd bring that new act in every week, you know, and it was quite an experience for me. Course I could read, but it was a big town and then I began to hear guys. There was a guy like Lorenzo Lawson, he was a top tenor player in Detroit, and Moon Mullins and Lamont...and so I was gettin' around a little bit then and there was a joint where we could go and jam and then when the guys would…

taps, he had on his shoes. And it...ohhh...I'd never heard anything like that before in my life, getting into sound. Everybody had their head down and this man was tap dancin' on the sidewalk, up side the walls, over the fire hydrants and whatnot. I say, "Who in the world is this?" They said, "This is Baby Lawrence." I says, "My God!" Can you imagine a couple hundred people congregated in a corner and they ain't nobody sayin' nuthin' and listenin' to Baby Lawrence dance. Ohhhh!
